Class AmwpCodec

java.lang.Object
org.aetheris.wire.AmwpCodec
public final class AmwpCodec extends Object
The AmwpCodec class encodes and decodes AMWP frames. AMWP is the framed protocol on the connection. A multi-byte integer is little-endian. The class does not decode the framed stream as UTF-8. // @aa-sdd G-07 G-18 aetheris-stages-1-3.finalize.md

  • Method Details

    • encode

      public static byte[] encode(int channel, int type, int flags, byte[] payload)
      The method builds one frame as a header plus the payload. A null payload is encoded as an empty body. A body longer than AmwpConstants.MAX_PAYLOAD throws IllegalArgumentException. The header is 16 bytes. Byte 0 is the magic value. Byte 1 is the version. Bytes 2 and 3 are the channel. Byte 4 is the type. Byte 5 is the flags. Bytes 6 and 7 are zero. Bytes 8 through 11 are the payload length. Bytes 12 through 15 are the CRC32C of the first 12 header bytes plus the body.
      Parameters:
      channel - The channel is the frame channel id.
      type - The type is the frame type byte.
      flags - The flags are the frame flag byte.
      payload - The payload is the body octets, and it may be null.
      Returns:
      The return value is the 16-byte header followed by the payload.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - The method throws this when the payload is longer than 1 mebibyte.

    • write

      public static void write(OutputStream out, int channel, int type, int flags, byte[] payload) throws IOException
      The method writes one encoded frame and flushes the stream.
      Parameters:
      out - The stream is the sink that receives the frame.
      channel - The channel is the frame channel id.
      type - The type is the frame type byte.
      flags - The flags are the frame flag byte.
      payload - The payload is the body octets, and it may be null.
      Throws:
      IOException - The method throws this when the write or the flush fails.

    • read

      public static AmwpFrame read(InputStream in) throws IOException
      The method blocks until one frame is read. End of stream before the first byte returns null. Any later short read is a truncated frame.
      Parameters:
      in - The stream is the framed byte stream.
      Returns:
      The return value is the frame, or null on a clean end of stream.
      Throws:
      IOException - The method throws this when the frame is truncated or corrupt.

    • parse

      public static AmwpFrame parse(byte[] header, InputStream in) throws IOException
      The method parses a 16-byte header and reads the payload from the stream. A null header throws IOException. A header shorter than 16 bytes throws IOException. A magic byte other than 0xAE throws IOException. A version other than 1 throws IOException. A payload length below 0 or above AmwpConstants.MAX_PAYLOAD throws IOException. A CRC32C that does not match the header throws IOException. The checksum covers the first 12 header bytes and the payload.
      Parameters:
      header - The header is the 16-byte header, with byte 0 already filled.
      in - The stream supplies the payload bytes.
      Returns:
      The return value is the decoded frame.
      Throws:
      IOException - The method throws this when the header or the payload is corrupt.

      public static boolean isMagic(int b)
      The method reports whether a byte is the AMWP magic value. The comparison uses the low 8 bits.
      Parameters:

      Returns:

    • scopeAPayload

      public static byte[] scopeAPayload(int fragIndex, int fragCount, byte[] cellId, byte[] body)
      The method builds a Scope A payload. Scope A is channel A, the notebook channel. The prefix is AmwpConstants.FRAG_PREFIX_BYTES bytes. The first 4 bytes are the fragment index. The next 4 bytes are the fragment count. The next 16 bytes are the cell id. A null cell id, or an id whose length is not 16, is stored as 16 zero bytes. A null body is stored as empty. The body follows the prefix.
      Parameters:
      fragIndex - The index is the fragment number.
      fragCount - The count is how many fragments make the message.
      cellId - The cell id is 16 bytes, or null.
      body - The body is the remaining octets, and it may be null.
      Returns:
      The return value is the prefix followed by the body.

    • fits

      public static boolean fits(byte[] body)
      The method reports whether a Scope A body fits in one frame. The measured length is AmwpConstants.FRAG_PREFIX_BYTES plus the body length. A null body counts as length 0. The method does not call encode(int, int, int, byte[]), so it does not throw for a long body.
      Parameters:
      body - The body is the reply bytes without the fragment prefix, and it may be null.
      Returns:
      The return value is true when that total is at most AmwpConstants.MAX_PAYLOAD.

    • stripFragPrefix

      public static byte[] stripFragPrefix(byte[] payload)
      The method returns the body after the Scope A fragment prefix. A null payload returns a new empty array. A payload shorter than AmwpConstants.FRAG_PREFIX_BYTES is returned unchanged.
      Parameters:
      payload - The payload is a Scope A payload, and it may be null.
      Returns:
      The return value is the body, or the original payload when it is too short.

    • cellIdOf

      public static byte[] cellIdOf(byte[] payload)
      The method copies the 16-byte cell id from a Scope A payload. The id starts at offset 8. A null payload returns 16 zero bytes. A payload shorter than the fragment prefix returns 16 zero bytes.
      Parameters:
      payload - The payload is a Scope A payload, and it may be null.
      Returns:
      The return value is a new 16-byte array.
